sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund Wilhelm. 1854. Polyglotta Africana; or, A comparative vocabulary of nearly three hundred words and phrases in more than one hundred distinct African languages. London: Church Missionary House. Preface p. vi; Introductory Remarks p. 20 (no. XII.B.21 'Afudu or Afaru'); Afudu column no. 21 in the vocabulary tables.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No language-specific statement. Preface p. vi lists the notation for the whole book: '´ the common sign for the accent, e.g., á, ó.' The Afudu column carries acute marks on many items (e.g. printed p. 3: one 'do & kádo', two 'mbéfe & béfai', three 'mbétori & bétori'), but nothing says what the accent is or where it falls. The p. 20 notice is an informant biography (Abitso/John Second of Bititi near Betson, capital burnt by 'Beliyi or Bedeyi'; countrymen in Sierra Leone 'some of whom have quite forgotten their language').

The Atlas is an entry list; the only Afudu locus in the whole 2020 text (a full-text search for stress/accent Afudu/Afuru/Yaffuda: 1 hit) is the alphabetical cross-reference 'Afudu – dialect of Tangale' (printed p. 3). The Tangale entry (431: Chadic, West A, Bole-Tangale; dialects 'Ture, Kaltungo, Shongom, Billiri'; refs incl. 'Phonology: Kidda-Awak (1993)') does not list Afudu among its dialects and says nothing about Koelle's language. No stress, accent or tone statement for Afudu anywhere; the 3rd edition carries the identical single line (PDF p. 16).

sources.note: No phonology content. Verbatim (p. 188): 'Groups D (S.-B.) and E (S.-B.) still remain tantalisingly unconfirmed, beyond Koelle's record of them in the early fifties.. Mr. Meek (Secretary to the Northern Nigerian Government) thinks that Afudu is spoken in the Nassarawa province north of the Western Benue. But Koelle's geographical indications are in favour of a location immediately south of the Central Benue. Afudu shows some sign of distant affinity with its nearest neighbour, Munsi. It is by no means specially related to Boritsu, or Mbarike, though placed near them by Koelle.'
